purpose: Constants FROZEN BEFORE the out-of-sample arc run of 2026-08-22. Committed first so the prediction model cannot be tuned to the run it is scored against; re-fitting after the run would prove nothing, exactly as moving a threshold after seeing the data proves nothing.
model: v = k_lin * linear_speed; w = k_ang * angular_speed; integrated as a circular arc of radius v/w from the mirror-derived facing at the interval start
k_lin_source: 16 steady-state in-window steps across three straight captures (4 s Phase 1, 8 s sustain, guard run), first interval of each dropped as spin-up plus feed-lag unwind
k_ang_source: the single angular-180 shallow-arc capture of 2026-08-22, 3 steps. IN-SAMPLE for that run and therefore the thing this out-of-sample test exists to check.
scored_against: an arc at a DIFFERENT angular_speed, never 180

planned_run.why_gentler_not_tighter: scripts/freeze_phase1_corridors.py sizes its arc lateral allowance from the measured angular-180 radius, so it UNDER-estimates the drift of a tighter arc. Going gentler than 180 keeps the real path inside a corridor validated for a tighter one.

pass_criteria_proposed_not_frozen.basis: two thirds of the 0.15 m waypoint tolerance, leaving a third for the steering law and sensing floor; see docs/phase1-criterion-revision-proposal-20260822.md
pass_criteria_proposed_not_frozen.note: steady-state steps only; the first interval of a window mixes dispatch latency, drivetrain ramp and ~1 s feed staleness and cannot be separated with one sample per run
